questions.question: If you have a passenger on your motorcycle, which is NOT something you should do?

options.text: Ride slower than usual.
Leave more distance to stop than usual.
Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle with a passenger handles differently because of the extra weight. Ride slower and allow more stopping distance. The passenger should grip the passenger handgrips or hold your waist, hips, or midsection firmly.

questions.question: When reacting to a hazard in the road, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Avoid communicating with other drivers.
Adjust your speed as needed.
Use your horn and lights or signals to alert others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid communicating with other drivers.
questions.explanation: Alert other drivers by using your horn, lights, and signals. Adjust your speed for the situation. Change your lane position or direction if needed.

questions.question: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should:

options.text: Create an angle of 45 to 90 degrees with the curb.
Be parked without a wheel or fender touching the curb.
Be parked parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Create an angle of 45 to 90 degrees with the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 45 to 90 degree angle to the curb. A wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To avoid a hazard, press lightly on the handgrip on the side where you want to escape.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, you:

options.text: May exceed the speed limit by 10 mph.
Must not exceed the speed limit.
Are required to ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must not exceed the speed limit.
questions.explanation: Always pass within the posted speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may proceed with caution.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. Stop completely and wait for a signal that lets you turn the way you want to go.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a divided roadway is ahead.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Get off the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: In rain, do not ride in the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks of cars ahead of you. The left track is often best, but this depends on traffic and conditions.

questions.question: Before riding with a passenger, tell them to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before you do.
Sit as far back as possible.
Hold your waist, hips, or belt firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold your waist, hips, or belt firmly.
questions.explanation: Have your passenger wait until you start the engine before getting on. They should sit as far forward as comfortable and grip your waist, hips, or belt firmly.

questions.question: When riding in a group, how much distance should be between the lead rider and the rider behind them?

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds
questions.explanation: In a staggered group formation under normal conditions, keep a three-second following distance between you and the rider in front of you.

questions.question: When riding over scored pavement in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Look down to see the changes in the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Stay to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: When riding over scored pavement, keep your head and eyes up. Ride slowly, keep a steady throttle, and do not fight the handlebars.

questions.question: Before starting out, you should make sure the fuel valve is:

options.text: Open.
Closed.
Covered.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open.
questions.explanation: Before you ride, make sure your fuel valve is open. If it is closed, the engine may start using fuel left in the lines, but it will stop once those lines are empty.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Provide you with an escape route.
Help you receive wind blasts.
Communicate your intentions to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you receive wind blasts.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage others from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: A "wobble," or sudden shaking of the front wheel and handlebars, is usually caused by:

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
Improperly tightening the front wheel to the frame.
Hitting an object with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
questions.explanation: A wobble is when the front wheel and handlebars shake from side to side. Most wobbles happen because of improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: Part of your normal scanning routine while riding should include:

options.text: Constantly looking in the rearview mirror.
Frequent rearview mirror checks.
Not using the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Frequent rearview mirror checks.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while riding. Use them especially when changing lanes, stopping at an intersection, or slowing down.

questions.question: One problem with riding directly next to another vehicle is that:

options.text: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
The other vehicle can easily see you.
You may not be able to read road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. The vehicle could swerve into your lane and hit you. It could also block your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop your motorcycle until the dog loses interest.
Approach the dog slowly, then quickly accelerate away as it gets close.
Swerve around the dog.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the dog slowly, then quickly accelerate away as it gets close.
questions.explanation: If a dog approaches, slow down and downshift until you are close to it. Then quickly accelerate away from the dog.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid an obstacle on the road, you should:

options.text: Speed up before hitting the object.
Stay seated so the seat cushions the impact.
Try to approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle, slow down and approach it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.question: When taking a curve while riding in a group, you should be in:

options.text: A single-file formation.
Pairs.
A staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: A single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Groups normally ride in a staggered formation. Change to single-file when taking a curve, making a turn, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: You may go faster than the speed limit until you finish passing.
You may pass in a no passing zone if you started the pass in a passing zone.
You must follow the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must follow the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must complete all passes at or below the posted speed limit. You may only pass in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: What is a difference between goggles and a windshield?

options.text: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
A windshield protects your eyes from wind, but goggles do not.
A windshield prevents your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from wind. Most windshields do not. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
Only slow down to let other traffic pass.
Other vehicles may enter the roadway ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely. Let all crossing traffic and pedestrians pass. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Is it good to use all three lane positions?

options.text: No, because you will never get used to any part of a lane.
No, because it will confuse other drivers.
Yes, if road and traffic conditions are changing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if road and traffic conditions are changing.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When turning, what should you do?

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn your head only (not your shoulders) to look through the turn.
Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head only (not your shoulders) to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, look toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon. Turning your shoulders can cause you to steer off course.
